_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); hotel signals

pit_profile.why: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'At year-end 2011, our system was comprised of 3,718 properties (643,196 rooms)'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties for customers'; 'General economic uncertainty and weak demand in the lodging industry could continue to impact our financial results and growth'; 'Conditions for our lodging business improved in 2011 reflecting generally low supply growth, a more favorable economic climate in most developed markets around the world, albeit at a generally low growth rate, and stronger economic growth in emerging markets, strong unit growth, and the impact of operating efficiencies across our company'; and 'we completed a spin-off of our timeshare operations and timeshare development business through a special tax-free dividend to our shareholders' (its own FY2011 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it

classification.quality_note: Marriott: 'Consistent with our focus on management, franchising, and licensing, we own very few of our lodging properties'; 'At year-end 2011, our system was comprised of 3,718 properties (643,196 rooms)'; 'Our industry is highly competitive, which may impact our ability to compete successfully with other hotel properties for customers'; 'General economic uncertainty and weak demand in the lodging industry could continue to impact our financial results and growth'; 'Conditions for our lodging business improved in 2011 reflecting generally low supply growth, a more favorable economic climate in most developed markets around the world, albeit at a generally low growth rate, and stronger economic growth in emerging markets, strong unit growth, and the impact of operating efficiencies across our company'; and 'we completed a spin-off of our timeshare operations and timeshare development business through a special tax-free dividend to our shareholders' (its own FY2011 10-K): a hotel management and franchise system whose fees follow the revenues and profits of its hotels through the economy, by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price fair; Ratio B 1.38x; +19% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.53; conservative 2yr +24%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -37.6%/yr (worst year FY02-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +11.5%/yr (Q1 fee guide + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +11.5%/yr (FY02-FY11 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +31.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY11); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: MAR (retrospective, 2012-03-02) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.38x (66.4% downside to Bear $12 / +48.3% upside to Bull $53) | Adj composite 2.85 vs market 2.32: gap +0.53 [UNDERVALUED] | +19% above the EPP floor $30 (19x FY12E $1.58) | Conservative 2-yr case: +24.2% total (+12.1%/yr) | At 22.6x FY12E the 15% hurdle price $47 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; North American RevPAR +6.2% in Q4 2011, forward fee revenue +5.73-9.32% (Q1 2012 fee revenue guide); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
